title: Independent VFX Research Reference
status: Independent evidence input; not final cross-model synthesis; no agent implementation
methodology: Tiers: A is first-hand maker writing/talks, peer-reviewed research or clearly labeled preprints; Spec is Roblox Creator Docs; B is strong trade reporting with named makers; C is named expert teaching/community evidence. Tier D is not used as proof.

Evidence levels: study, preprint, industry practice, spec and inference. These are claim labels, not a single confidence score. A source may support a capability or observation without validating a proposed recipe.
Recency: modern sources are preferred. Retained pre-2020 classics are marked and linked to a newer qualification or an explicit follow-up gap. Catalog pages support metadata and stated scope only.

Numbers retain units, sample, timebase and task context. Inferred arithmetic is labeled. Missing values are “no number found” or null in the card template, never fabricated defaults. Tier C-only precision carries an explicit corroboration limit.

Every artist-derived feeling is a design hypothesis unless measured. No unconditional player-over-enemy hierarchy, universal layer count or fixed mobile particle budget was established. The most important actionable cue may be an edge rather than the brightest center.
Quotations were avoided; field terms and source titles are retained. The later synthesis should reconcile disagreements at the claim level and preserve contrary/null findings.

intro: All 54 recipes are proposed inferences assembled from the component principles. They are not measurements of the named films or games. Importance is relative to the player’s next decision; no unsupported numerical rating or phase duration is assigned.

Windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through and dissipation are available phases, not a requirement that every effect contain all five. Authoritative activation/contact/expiry wins over cosmetic timing. A rarity ladder is a proposed project convention, not evidence of an optimal reward or monetization design.

outputs.title: Scene placement rulebook

rules.rule: Make the actionable edge match gameplay geometry.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Overlay collision/area debug view on the primary indicator at cast, impact and expiry; flag mismatches separately from decorative overflow.

rules.rule: Assign importance separately for each viewer role.
rules.numbers: 1–10 is reported League practice; exact scale singly sourced.
rules.pass_fail: Record caster/enemy/ally priorities and the decision each visible cue supports.

rules.rule: Let the current actionable threat beat irrelevant spectacle.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Ask testers what they must react to while reward, ambient and ally effects run; record wrong-target reactions.

rules.rule: Keep a recognisable primary shape across variants.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Blind-test ability identity for base/skin/recolour variants; reject a variant that changes the inferred action.

rules.rule: Make projectile direction readable when paused.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Pause at several positions and ask travel direction; inspect head–tail ambiguity.

rules.rule: Remove irrelevant viewer-specific cues.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: For each layer, document whose next action would change if it vanished; omit only genuinely noninformative variants.

rules.rule: Reserve value and saturation headroom across the whole scene.
rules.numbers: no number found for universal brightness ratios or HSV bands.
rules.pass_fail: Inspect scene/character/VFX/UI simultaneously; identify unintended competitors at the moment of decision.

rules.rule: Use the stage to support the effect.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Replay on brightest, darkest and most patterned permitted surfaces; adjust the background or effect contrast if recognition fails.

rules.rule: Move ornament away from gameplay sightlines where possible.
rules.numbers: VALORANT reports most details above player height; no universal pixel-height rule.
rules.pass_fail: Check expected target/path screen regions under the actual camera; reduce decorative contrast in those regions.

rules.rule: Budget overlap by decision performance, not emitter count alone.
rules.numbers: no number found for universal count, coverage or overdraw threshold.
rules.pass_fail: Run worst credible multiplayer overlaps on target phones; measure detection errors, response time, screen occlusion and GPU cost together.

rules.rule: Retire active hazard language when the hazard ends.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Stop on the final damage/status tick and inspect the remaining border/colour/motion; residue must not imply another hit.

rules.rule: Lower the prominence of aftermath.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Compare peak and residue under competing threats; flag residual smoke/light that attracts attention away from a new actionable cue.

rules.rule: Check effects while the player is looking elsewhere.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Use a central tracking task plus peripheral warning; repeat at actual phone display size and camera distance.

rules.rule: Treat surprise onsets as a shared scene resource.
rules.numbers: no number found for a safe onset interval.
rules.pass_fail: Compare isolated and rapid overlapping bursts while targets move; record missed warnings and tracking loss.

rules.rule: Do not assume the brightest pixel wins.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Use eye tracking when available, otherwise timed recognition/choice tests; compare intended focus with observed choices.

rules.rule: Keep hit confirmation semantically distinct from firing.
rules.numbers: VALORANT example 80 ms plus processing from 40 ms one-way; not a Roblox budget.
rules.pass_fail: Test misses, predicted hits rejected by server, late confirmations and moving/crouching targets.

rules.rule: Check screen effects with player control active.
rules.numbers: no number found for universal shake amplitude, frequency or duration.
rules.pass_fail: Test aim, camera turn, jump/path navigation during kick/shake/zoom; retest with reduced effects.

rules.rule: Match the timing style to the gameplay contract.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Log cast/contact/peak/last-active/last-visible timestamps in milliseconds; do not add cosmetic delay to a required instant response.

rules.rule: Build temporal contrast at scene level.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Compare ordinary play, buildup, payoff and aftermath; check that ordinary repeats have not consumed every available prominence cue.

rules.rule: Keep depth cues useful.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Review foreground particles, camera-near cards, fog and depth of field; confirm all required target/path cues remain available.

rules.rule: Test the composition with optional polish removed.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Disable bloom/world light/camera layers and inspect whether identity, hit extent and phase remain understandable.

rules.rule: Do not import film staging as a compulsory gameplay cut.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: For a cinematic payoff, verify whether control and threats are intentionally paused; otherwise keep the gameplay view usable.

rules.rule: Calibrate screen measurements before interpreting them.
rules.numbers: duration_ms=1000×frames/fps; arithmetic conversion, not a tuning recommendation.
rules.pass_fail: Record viewport resolution, device, camera FOV/distance, capture frame rate and display frame rate beside every coverage or timing measurement.

rules.rule: Use a single problem statement for each review change.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Record moment, viewer, symptom, probable cause, exact parameter edit, protected gameplay meaning and a comparison test.

rules.rule: Check that observers can distinguish an attempted action, successful hit, blocked hit and completed outcome with the selected effect build.
rules.numbers: no universal threshold found
rules.pass_fail: Fail when a miss reads as success or a success cue is hidden by the preceding action.

rules.rule: Randomise only decorative dimensions whose variation cannot change the meaning or timing of a gameplay cue.
rules.numbers: No supported universal rotation, hue, size, timing-jitter range or variant count found.
rules.pass_fail: Hold collision boundary, contact cue, team identity and warning deadline invariant.

rules.rule: Stress-test the repeated event at the game’s actual maximum cadence and realistic multiplayer concurrency.
rules.numbers: Use the brief’s 1,000-event replay as an automated durability workload, not a clinically safe human exposure prescription.
rules.pass_fail: Fail if tails accumulate, UI stops being readable, the next contact is masked, or frame-time budget fails.

rules.rule: Keep cheap input confirmation available when decorative repetition is capped or suppressed.
rules.numbers: No universal cooldown, cap or ducking percentage found.
rules.pass_fail: Fail if an accepted action becomes indistinguishable from dropped input.

rules.rule: Tie combo escalation to a readable change in achieved outcome, then test bounded progression against constant feedback.
rules.numbers: No sourced step count, escalation increment, reset time or maximum intensity found.
rules.pass_fail: Fail if spectacle makes separate hits or the streak-reset state ambiguous; do not assume more streak juice raises retention.

rules.rule: Author one contact event that schedules the visual punch and sound transient together; measure actual output synchrony.
rules.numbers: No universal allowable game-impact delay found. Schedule from the same event, then measure displayed and audible output; no numerical offset default is prescribed.
rules.pass_fail: Check audio waveform onset against first visible contact/flash in captured output, including device latency and dropped frames.

rules.rule: Separate an intentional distant-explosion delay or anticipation sound from an accidental sync error.
rules.numbers: No universal sound-leading or picture-leading offset for hits found.
rules.pass_fail: The event card explicitly identifies the causal sync point and whether a nonzero offset is artistic/physical.

rules.rule: Assess the composite scene, including overlapping emitters, muzzle flashes, lighting, post effects, UI and camera movement.
rules.numbers: Evaluate every rolling 1-second interval; see SA01 criteria below.
rules.pass_fail: Per-asset passes are insufficient when the final combined output can exceed a criterion.

rules.rule: Do not use an accessibility toggle or seizure warning as the only response to known hazardous flashing.
rules.numbers: no number found
rules.pass_fail: Remove or redesign known failures before release; a player may encounter them before reaching settings.

rules.rule: Provide an off setting for nonessential camera shake, bob, motion blur and automatic camera movement.
rules.numbers: Halo Infinite example: separate 0–100% blur, shake, full-screen effect and speed-line controls. This scale specifies controls, not physical safe amplitude.
rules.pass_fail: Minimum setting fully removes the targeted nonessential motion; feedback remains interpretable.

rules.rule: Encode essential team, danger, rarity and state information with a non-colour signifier.
rules.numbers: At least one additional signifier: shape, pattern, icon or label.
rules.pass_fail: Correct interpretation remains possible without distinguishing the assigned hues; test with players, not simulation alone.

rules.rule: Use contrast ratios for important readable UI/markers, not as instructions to intensify every effect.
rules.numbers: XAG 102: standard important text/visual elements 4.5:1; large elements 3:1; high-contrast UI mode 7:1.
rules.pass_fail: Measure against the lowest-contrast local background; a glowing particle core does not certify the whole telegraph.

intro: Use these rules as observable checks. A number describes its stated source context only. When no transferable threshold exists, the pass/fail task replaces an invented screen percentage or particle cap.

case_studies.documented studio method: Map art is deliberately simplified and tested around player visibility.
case_studies.transfer inference: VFX review should include noisy and quiet backgrounds, not just a neutral showcase.
case_studies.limits: Environment policy does not guarantee effect legibility on its own.

case_studies.title: Overwatch 2
case_studies.documented studio method: Mythic skin presentation can differ by observer relationship.
case_studies.transfer inference: Separate cosmetic ownership from enemy-critical recognition.
case_studies.limits: Do not infer different hitboxes or damage indicators are acceptable.

case_studies.title: Rocksteady / Attention Overload
case_studies.documented studio method: Public session framing addresses combined-system readability.
case_studies.transfer inference: Use crowded encounter review as an acceptance condition.
case_studies.limits: Abstract-only supplemental case, not a fully reconstructed production method.

case_studies.title: Hi-Fi RUSH
case_studies.documented studio method: Rhythmic action and clean graphic rendering were explicit design goals.
case_studies.transfer inference: Bind accents to authorized gameplay/music clocks; compensate visual lead-in rather than adding arbitrary input latency.
case_studies.limits: Do not generalize its musical timing to non-rhythm combat.

case_studies.title: Balatro
case_studies.documented studio method: Creator describes tactile shader exploration and iterative juice.
case_studies.transfer inference: A reward chain should have a clear accumulation/result hierarchy even when animated elaborately.
case_studies.limits: Case establishes intention, not exactly how much shake, shader distortion or delay is effective.

case_studies.title: Hades
case_studies.documented studio method: Credited artist documents a deliberate move toward bold immediate expression.
case_studies.transfer inference: Use the aesthetic goal as a comparison prompt for a candidate effect, not a numeric recipe.
case_studies.limits: Detailed current maker evidence for Hades VFX construction is insufficient in this pass.

case_studies.title: Teardown
case_studies.documented studio method: Destruction is a route-planning and heist-execution mechanic, not merely an explosion layer.
case_studies.transfer inference: Validate new sightlines, paths and traversability before polishing dust.
case_studies.limits: No attempt here to recreate its voxel solver or claim sprite VFX provide equivalent destruction.

case_studies.title: THE FINALS
case_studies.documented studio method: Authored prefractured buildings retain interior/collision quality; damage presentation is tuned for accurate judgment.
case_studies.transfer inference: Drive dust/debris from real fracture events; reveal the final breach and retained cover.
case_studies.limits: A prefractured asset is not proof that every break is scripted; physical collapse and authoring are separate stages.

case_studies.title: Battlefield 6
case_studies.documented studio method: Systemic breakage is shaped to leave playable ruins, with material-aware VFX/audio emission.
case_studies.transfer inference: Maintain one material/event vocabulary across particles, chunks, decals and sound; reconcile all with gameplay state.
case_studies.limits: Event schema proposed below is our synthesis, not copied engine architecture.

case_studies.title: Rainbow Six Siege
case_studies.documented studio method: Classic implementation distinguishes procedural wall damage and lightweight decorative fragments.
case_studies.transfer inference: Budget meaningful cover separately from cheap, short-lived debris dressing.
case_studies.limits: 2016 technical details cannot be assumed unchanged in Siege X; 2025 source confirms only ongoing strategic environmental destruction.
case_studies.mechanism: Procedural cutting + authored cosmetic debris; historical implementation

case_studies.title: Spider-Verse, original and sequel
case_studies.documented studio method: Reusable graphic ingredients and stepped motion are documented; sequel increased bespoke shot work.
case_studies.transfer inference: A library-based agent should expose a ceiling: adapt compatible ingredients, or flag that a new asset is needed for a hero contour.
case_studies.limits: Per-component film cadence is not a license to desynchronize gameplay/contact; art-directed camera privileges do not automatically transfer.
case_studies.mechanism: Offline 2D/3D compositing, simulations and variable sampling

case_studies.title: Turning Red
case_studies.documented studio method: Graphic poofs use designed breakup; other hand-painted elements avoid simulation entirely.
case_studies.transfer inference: Choose opacity, breakup and flow as separate controls when the available asset permits them.
case_studies.limits: Replaying a breakup texture approximates authored appearance; it does not implement Pixar’s subdivision or fluid tools.
case_studies.mechanism: Offline hybrid: hand-painted elements and stylized simulation

case_studies.title: The Bad Guys
case_studies.documented studio method: Library sprites and procedural work share an intentionally illustrated visual vocabulary.
case_studies.transfer inference: Reject a photoreal smoke card inside a flat graphic effect unless a deliberate style bridge exists.
case_studies.limits: Do not assume merely stacking sprites hides the medium boundary automatically.
case_studies.mechanism: Offline sprite / simulation / drawn overlay hybrid

case_studies.title: Puss in Boots: The Last Wish
case_studies.documented studio method: Action timing, lighting and background simplification were coordinated.
case_studies.transfer inference: Protect the action silhouette at the visual peak; keep post effects optional and context-specific.
case_studies.limits: No one cadence applies to the whole film; article describes stepped action but supplies no universal frame count.
case_studies.mechanism: Offline stylized rendering and action animation

case_studies.title: Arcane
case_studies.documented studio method: Drawn overlays complement shot-led animation and graphic composition.
case_studies.transfer inference: Use authored overlays as state-specific accents, while maintaining independent player-readable cues.
case_studies.limits: Do not call all Arcane effects 2D or claim a uniform stepped rate from this source.
case_studies.mechanism: Offline drawn overlays over CG plates

case_studies.title: Dune
case_studies.documented studio method: Layered coarse motion and fine granular/dust detail sell worm-driven sand displacement.
case_studies.transfer inference: For a cheap ground rupture, preserve origin, travel direction, material mass and residual dust as separate roles.
case_studies.limits: This recipe is a visual approximation; it cannot reproduce interactive sand volume or structural displacement.

case_studies.title: Oppenheimer
case_studies.documented studio method: Practical photographic elements are selected, retimed and composited.
case_studies.transfer inference: Kitbashing quality depends on shared timing/perspective/lighting, not whether source pieces were simulated or filmed.
case_studies.limits: Real-time camera freedom breaks some film compositing cheats; inspect from playable views.

case_studies.title: Godzilla Minus One
case_studies.documented studio method: Damage respects underlying materials and camera framing supplies human scale.
case_studies.transfer inference: For a giant strike, ensure observers can read a scale anchor, material response and surviving environment.
case_studies.limits: Do not copy film occlusion or camera takeover into competitive play by default.

case_studies.title: Demon Slayer / ufotable
case_studies.documented studio method: Graphic water was developed through references and CG/hand-drawn cooperation.
case_studies.transfer inference: Use a coherent family of stylized shapes across charge, travel and contact.
case_studies.limits: A single article does not document every season or every breathing style.

case_studies.title: Chainsaw Man / Benjamin Faure shot examples
case_studies.documented studio method: Artist describes deliberate departures from filmed reference and redraw of stepped CG props.
case_studies.transfer inference: Reference should inform causality but does not prohibit exaggerating the readable silhouette.
case_studies.limits: Personal shot-level evidence; not a studio-wide formula.

case_studies.title: Yoshimichi Kameda craft interview
case_studies.documented studio method: Artist explains graphic impact imagery and staging across multiple productions.
case_studies.transfer inference: Borrow rare-event contrast and strong composition, subject to accessibility and contextual testing.
case_studies.limits: Retrospective mixes production eras; no empirical flash recipe.

case_studies.title: Beyond the Dark Creature
case_studies.documented studio method: Official sample uses selected glow areas and anatomy-local smoke.
case_studies.transfer inference: A prefab needs correct anchors and focal priorities in addition to attractive textures.
case_studies.limits: Worked example, not evidence for Blox Fruits, DOORS or Pet Simulator pipelines.
case_studies.mechanism: Real-time Roblox mesh / light / particle composition

case_studies.title: Island Jump goal flare and atmosphere
case_studies.documented studio method: Official tutorial separates goal-oriented movement from ambient particles.
case_studies.transfer inference: Give goal and ambience different priority and visibility rules.
case_studies.limits: Only two well-documented Roblox examples found; do not inflate this into three commercial studio case studies.

intro: Use documented production methods as references for staging and asset selection. A film frame can be tightly controlled; an interactive multiplayer scene cannot assume the same camera, timing or occlusion tolerance. Coverage gaps are retained rather than filled with famous titles or fan analysis.

outputs.title: Juice and satisfaction table

rows.quality or finding: Success-linked feedback, rather than mere amplification
rows.why it works (or fails): In the preregistered RPG experiment, outcomes mattered; occlusion is a proposed mechanism, not an isolated manipulation.
rows.effect size if known: n=1,699. Success-dependence → competence +.45 [95% CI .30,.60]; effectance +.26 [.15,.36]; curiosity +.29 [.17,.41]. Unstandardised scale-point coefficients.
rows.evidence level: study; JS01, A, 2024, Fig.4

rows.why it works (or fails): Tested non-success-dependent glow hid repeated impacts.
rows.how to make it: Audit action–outcome legibility before increasing volume.
rows.effect size if known: Amplification → effectance −.19 [−.36,−.03]; competence −.43 [−.68,−.19]. No significant direct enjoyment/playtime effect.
rows.evidence level: study; JS01, A, 2024

rows.quality or finding: Random variety is not established retention
rows.why it works (or fails): Variability did not significantly predict curiosity or playtime.
rows.how to make it: Use variation for appearance; test behavioural benefit.
rows.evidence level: study; JS01, A, 2024

rows.quality or finding: An intermediate amount can beat extremes
rows.why it works (or fails): One RPG bundled audiovisual changes, rather than isolating a particle setting.
rows.how to make it: Compare complete builds; no transferable medium/high particle budget.
rows.effect size if known: n=3,018. Partial η²: competence .005; autonomy .004; immersion .003; enjoyment .006; playtime .006; character level .006.
rows.evidence level: study; JS02, A, 2020

rows.why it works (or fails): None and Extreme both lost on playtime; enjoyment pairwise significance was Extreme < Medium/High, not None < Medium/High.
rows.how to make it: Do not equate statistical significance with a large retention improvement.
rows.effect size if known: Playtime F(3,3014)=5.83, p<.001; enjoyment F(3,3014)=5.87, p<.001. No numeric pairwise retention uplift found.
rows.evidence level: study; JS02, A, 2020, §6

rows.quality or finding: Impact-feel features are candidates, not proven causes
rows.why it works (or fails): Review-derived game ranking plus descriptive feature inventory cannot isolate causes.
rows.how to make it: Test hit-stop, sound coherence and camera control separately.
rows.effect size if known: 281,720 Chinese reviews; 96 games, filtered to 44, then top/bottom 8 each. No causal effect size or feature correlation coefficient found.
rows.evidence level: preprint; JS03, A, 2022; later IEEE GEM publication verified

rows.why it works (or fails): In a minimal targeting task, words communicated graded performance more clearly.
rows.how to make it: Use readable success/outcome labels when needed; preserve meaning without particles.
rows.effect size if known: n=45; progress-feedback omnibus Kendall’s W=.44; means Text 5.62, Particles 4.43, None 2.81 (7-point scale).
rows.evidence level: study; JS04, A, 2024, Table 2

rows.why it works (or fails): No overall superiority of text over juicy particles; observation/performance stages showed no significant performance differences.
rows.how to make it: Treat onomatopoeia as an optional style layer, not universal upgrade.
rows.effect size if known: Study effects lasted 0.5 s; this is stimulus duration, not optimal lifetime.

rows.why it works (or fails): Interviewed audio designers reserve standout moments, vary repetition and align sounds with visible events.
rows.how to make it: Keep frequent feedback restrained; let sound carry some impact.
rows.effect size if known: 12 expert interviews; no causal effect size, optimal variant count or repetition threshold found.
rows.evidence level: study (qualitative); JS05, A, 2024

rows.quality or finding: Completion, fitting and clean endings as design targets
rows.why it works (or fails): Plausible perceptual/semantic goals; this search did not establish an effect-size recipe for them.
rows.how to make it: Specify an unambiguous terminal state and test whether it reads as complete.
rows.game uses: Coin counters, unlocks, assembly, UI success
rows.evidence level: inference; requires validation

intro: The best-supported conclusion is conditional: feedback must preserve action and outcome information. More decoration is not a universal route to enjoyment or motivation. Experimental effect sizes refer to the tested builds and samples.

outputs.title: Mistakes table

rows.why it looks bad: The effect teaches an incorrect safe/unsafe boundary.
rows.how to spot it: Overlay authoritative geometry through the full active interval.
rows.fix: Correct the primary border before changing decoration; check every variant. [industry practice: ES-S01]

rows.why it looks bad: Prominence stops predicting consequence.
rows.how to spot it: Show ordinary/critical/ultimate events together and ask which matters.
rows.fix: Reassign relative hierarchy; trim ordinary peaks rather than endlessly enlarging the ultimate. [inference from ES-S02]

rows.why it looks bad: The eye follows decoration instead of collision.
rows.how to spot it: Pause and identify the damaging part.
rows.fix: Demote trail value/opacity/detail and clarify the head. [industry practice: ES-S04]

rows.why it looks bad: Meaning and motion direction become ambiguous.
rows.how to spot it: Remove each layer individually and compare identification.
rows.fix: Keep components with a specific role; replace conflicting silhouettes. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Internal structure and nearby targets disappear.
rows.how to spot it: Inspect normal and grayscale captures with bloom toggled.
rows.fix: Reduce broad glow first; localize the peak and preserve dark/light structure. [inference]

rows.mistake: Pretty in isolation, invisible in play
rows.why it looks bad: Preview background concealed a context problem.
rows.how to spot it: Replay in actual maps/cameras with opponents and UI.
rows.fix: Adjust contrast/shape or stage support, then retest; more saturation is not always sufficient. [industry practice: ES-S07, ES-S09]

rows.why it looks bad: The primary shape becomes shimmer or noise.
rows.how to spot it: View at real projected size during movement.
rows.fix: Select a coarser silhouette, shorten small debris tails or remove tertiary detail. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Equal rates obscure acceleration and release.
rows.how to spot it: Plot size/speed/value over time and inspect main transitions.
rows.fix: Retune the dominant parameter first; preserve deliberately constant projectiles. [inference from ES-S07]

rows.mistake: Extra swelling before an instant impact
rows.why it looks bad: A response reads as late or soft.
rows.how to spot it: Compare gameplay contact timestamp with the visible peak.
rows.fix: Start at a suitable energetic flipbook frame or choose another asset; do not move the gameplay hit casually. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Complexity collapses into one unreadable mass.
rows.how to spot it: Solo the core and compare the combined first peak.
rows.fix: Offset only secondary motion/dissipation while preserving contact alignment. [industry practice: ES-S09]

rows.why it looks bad: The player may keep avoiding a harmless area.
rows.how to spot it: Review the final active tick alongside the remaining visual.
rows.fix: End the semantic hazard cue; retain only clearly different residue if useful. [inference]

rows.mistake: Uniform opacity fade on an asset needing breakup
rows.why it looks bad: The silhouette can look like a flat card being switched off.
rows.how to spot it: Watch the tail against both light and dark surfaces.
rows.fix: Select a breakup flipbook or size/shape tail; retain simple fades when they read better. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Variants imply different reach, intensity or direction.
rows.how to spot it: Compare extremes of randomized settings.
rows.fix: Randomize ornamental parameters inside tested bounds; lock semantic geometry and event timing. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Vocabulary loses reliability.
rows.how to spot it: Ask new players to classify unknown examples.
rows.fix: Define colour plus shape/motion roles and correct exceptions. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Feedback consumes control or visibility.
rows.how to spot it: Aim/navigate during the effect rather than watching a reel.
rows.fix: Lower/remove the troublesome layer and offer reduced camera effects. [inference]

rows.mistake: Late body-hit effect appears on the head
rows.why it looks bad: Correct simulation looks incorrect.
rows.how to spot it: Frame-step a moving/crouching target with latency telemetry.
rows.fix: Use body-part-specific confirmation/attachment only after testing occlusion trade-offs. [industry practice: ES-S18]

rows.why it looks bad: An impressive shader cannot clarify the event sequence.
rows.how to spot it: Replace appearance with simple grayscale parts.
rows.fix: Fix event shape/timing before restoring polish. [industry practice: ES-S10, ES-S09]

rows.mistake: A laboratory number becomes an aesthetic default
rows.why it looks bad: The task/display/population changed.
rows.how to spot it: Inspect each numeric field’s source and context.
rows.fix: Keep study outcomes in evidence fields; obtain game-specific test bounds. [inference]

rows.mistake: Calling a small p-value a large design gain
rows.why it looks bad: Statistical significance does not give magnitude or external validity.
rows.how to spot it: Check effect-size unit, confidence interval, game/sample and actual contrast.
rows.fix: Report the numeric effect and scope; do not promise a retention percentage.

rows.why it looks bad: Unpredictability can be meaningless.
rows.how to spot it: Player sees different colours but cannot learn anything useful.
rows.fix: Keep variation decorative or connect it to interpretable gameplay state.

rows.why it looks bad: Separates consequence from action.
rows.how to spot it: Compare earliest visible contact with audio and gameplay event.
rows.fix: Keep sync anchor fixed; vary tails/secondary details instead.

rows.mistake: Treating 25% as a whole-screen flashing allowance
rows.why it looks bad: Wrong geometry for WCAG’s visual-field criterion.
rows.how to spot it: Look for denominator and viewing-distance assumptions.
rows.fix: Use visual-field analysis and correct standards-aware tooling.

rows.mistake: A safety warning replacing a fix
rows.why it looks bad: Exposure can precede a player’s ability to disable the effect.
rows.how to spot it: Known failures still ship behind a splash screen.
rows.fix: Redesign failure and validate the composite output.

rows.why it looks bad: Lower decoration also deletes essential information.
rows.how to spot it: Play reduced-effects mode without sound.
rows.fix: Preserve or replace the semantic cue with a stable readable one.

rows.why it looks bad: People and contexts vary.
rows.how to spot it: Only simulation has been checked.
rows.fix: Use redundant signifiers, customization and actual player testing.

rows.mistake: Authoring timestamps treated as output sync
rows.why it looks bad: Display/audio pipelines add different delay.
rows.how to spot it: Code says simultaneous but a capture shows separation.
rows.fix: Measure emitted audio and displayed frames on target hardware.

rows.mistake: Using emission cap as scene budget
rows.why it looks bad: Often fails under overlapping effects and large transparent sprites
rows.how to spot it: Count seems legal but on-device GPU frame time spikes
rows.fix: Budget visible area/concurrency and measured CPU/GPU cost, preserving essential cue

rows.why it looks bad: Skips designed buildup or jumps straight into dissipation
rows.how to spot it: Event begins on inconsistent visual states
rows.fix: Disable random start for semantic one-shots; vary approved secondary elements instead

rows.why it looks bad: Smoke and volume disappear against bright backgrounds; overlap washes out hierarchy
rows.how to spot it: Inspect against bright stage and grayscale
rows.fix: Normal blending for obscuring mass; additive only for luminous portions

rows.why it looks bad: Muddies silhouette and increases overdraw
rows.how to spot it: Solo/mute each layer and name what information changes
rows.fix: Keep one primary read; remove redundant layers before adding detail

rows.mistake: Increasing sheet frames without checking cell resolution
rows.why it looks bad: More temporal detail can mean blurrier individual drawings
rows.how to spot it: Inspect per-cell artwork size and close-up phone capture
rows.fix: Choose fewer useful cells or a better-fitting aspect ratio; verify actual resident detail

rows.why it looks bad: Teleport streaks, stale particles or persistent glow appear
rows.how to spot it: Interrupt/reacquire rapidly and inspect the first new frame
rows.fix: Clear history, reset properties and callbacks; respect outstanding lifetime/TimeScale

rows.why it looks bad: Recipe cannot be implemented as written or substitution changes its meaning
rows.how to spot it: Property/class absent from current public API
rows.fix: Specify an honest approximation or request another approved asset; no invented API

rows.why it looks bad: A large flourish can contradict a minor outcome or hide that nothing changed; this is a design diagnosis, not a measured universal law.
rows.how to spot it: Compare the claimed importance with the actual state change; mute sound and remove tertiary layers.
rows.fix: Rebuild the primary contact/state cue, then add only a layer with a distinct job. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Uniform speeds and diffuse edges can fail to show where force was transferred.
rows.how to spot it: Scrub first contact and follow-through; check whether heavy pieces move like fine dust.
rows.fix: Concentrate contact timing and separate mass motion from decorative tails; test the revised feel. [inference; ES-S09]

intro: Diagnosis should identify the moment and symptom, then name a concrete change and a retest. These fixes are hypotheses constrained by the cited principles, not automatic guarantees of a better effect.

outputs.title: Roblox table

rows.key properties and values: Rate; Enabled; Lifetime; Emit(n); Clear()
rows.limits and mobile cost: 400/s per emitter; mobile 100/s. Lifetime cap 20 s. Screen area and overlap matter.
rows.best practice: Inference: explicit bursts for discrete impacts; choose count by measured cost and readability.

rows.key properties and values: None; 2×2/4×4/8×8; Custom via FlipbookSizeX/Y. Custom axes 1–64.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Texture dimensions must divide by grid; padding reduces bleed; unique sheets cost memory.
rows.best practice: Inference: record cell geometry and empty cells; reject incompatible assets.

rows.key properties and values: Loop, OneShot, PingPong, Random; fps ≤30; BlendFrames; StartRandom.
rows.limits and mobile cost: OneShot ignores fps; low-memory clients can disable flipbooks.
rows.best practice: Inference: retain authored first frame for important one-shots; blending off for held drawings.

rows.key properties and values: Color/Size/Transparency sequences; LightEmission 0 normal, 1 additive; LightInfluence 0–1; Brightness.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Emission does not light the scene. Brightness applies with LightInfluence=0.
rows.best practice: Inference: use separate local light only when world illumination adds needed information.

rows.what it is good for: Flow, elongation, layering, local slow motion
rows.key properties and values: Orientation; Rotation/RotSpeed; Squash; ZOffset; TimeScale 0–1.
rows.limits and mobile cost: ZOffset changes render depth, not geometry. No native per-frame-duration list found.
rows.best practice: Inference: use attachment transforms; record phase timing and cleanup explicitly.

rows.what it is good for: Shared origin and direction for effect layers
rows.key properties and values: CFrame, WorldCFrame; local position/orientation; links Beam/Trail endpoints.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Point emission differs from BasePart-volume emission. No safe instance count found.
rows.best practice: Inference: anchor to contact normal/muzzle/foot socket rather than eyeballing world offsets.

rows.what it is good for: Tethers, directional energy, arcs, continuous laser silhouettes
rows.key properties and values: Attachment0/1; Width0/1; CurveSize0/1; Segments; FaceCamera; texture controls.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Default Segments=10; at least n−1 for n keypoints. Overdraw still applies.
rows.best practice: Inference: minimal segment count that retains silhouette and sequences; endpoints match gameplay.

rows.what it is good for: Scrolling streak detail and emissive appearance
rows.key properties and values: TextureSpeed in cycles/s; Wrap/Static/Stretch; Brightness 0–10000, default 1.
rows.limits and mobile cost: LightEmission does not illuminate geometry; high brightness is not a design recommendation.
rows.best practice: Inference: use explicit units; recheck pattern speed after changing TextureLength/Mode.

rows.what it is good for: Sword swings, moving projectiles and motion history
rows.key properties and values: Attachment0/1; Lifetime 0.01–20 s (default 2); MinLength; MaxLength; WidthScale 0–1; Clear().
rows.limits and mobile cost: MaxLength=0 removes distance cap. Quality levels affect trail fidelity.
rows.best practice: Inference: clear pooled trail history before reuse/teleport; trim lifetime to avoid stale threat paths.

rows.key properties and values: Adornee; DepthMode AlwaysOnTop/Occluded; fill and outline colors/transparencies.
rows.limits and mobile cost: 255 client slots; disabled instances occupy slots; excess ignored.
rows.best practice: Inference: allocate by importance; destroy permanently retired highlights; avoid unintended through-wall information.

rows.key properties and values: Brightness, Color, Range, Shadows; direct BasePart/Attachment child.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Range ≤120 studs. Shadow cost grows with affected geometry/light density.
rows.best practice: Inference: choose shortest useful range; test shadowless version before adding shadows.

rows.key properties and values: Angle, Face, Range plus shared Light properties.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Range ≤120 studs; geometry and shadows determine cost; no universal light-count budget found.
rows.best practice: Inference: align with the actual action direction and keep gameplay visibility independent.

rows.what it is good for: Illuminated panels and broad surface glow
rows.key properties and values: Face, Angle, Range; behaves like SpotLight under Attachment.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Range ≤120 studs. A luminous texture is not a substitute for world lighting.
rows.best practice: Inference: prefer one purposeful source to overlapping redundant lights.

rows.what it is good for: Scene value/palette baseline and rendering intent
rows.key properties and values: LightingStyle Soft/Realistic; PrioritizeLightingQuality; Ambient, ExposureCompensation.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Technology is deprecated; quality priority trades shading against viewing distance.
rows.best practice: Inference: approve the environment first; tune VFX on all shipped lighting profiles.

rows.key properties and values: Density, Offset, Color, Decay, Glare, Haze.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Can obscure objects; poor Offset balance exposes ghosting or distant LOD popping. No universal safe density found.
rows.best practice: Inference: test distant threats against haze; do not use fog to conceal critical telegraphs.

rows.key properties and values: Intensity; Size in pixels; Threshold 0 all colors, 1 pure white.
rows.limits and mobile cost: May vary with quality; full-scene cost/readability interaction. No useful universal intensity number found.
rows.best practice: Inference: preserve the primary silhouette with bloom disabled.

rows.what it is good for: Defocusing the world behind a menu
rows.key properties and values: Size is Gaussian blur radius in pixels.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Global 3D blur; not radial/motion blur. Quality-dependent.
rows.best practice: Inference: avoid obscuring active danger during gameplay.

rows.what it is good for: Mood tint and localized player feedback
rows.key properties and values: Brightness −1 black/+1 white; Contrast; Saturation −1 grayscale; multiplicative TintColor.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Post effects do not alter GuiObjects; additive brightness may erase value structure.
rows.best practice: Inference: preserve HUD contrast separately and verify no-flash/reduced-effects variants.

rows.key properties and values: FocusDistance and InFocusRadius in studs; NearIntensity, FarIntensity.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Quality-dependent; can hide foreground/background threats. No safe intensity range found.
rows.best practice: Inference: reserve strong focus changes for moments without targeting demands.

rows.key properties and values: Intensity; Spread 0–1.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Not a general local volumetric-light beam. Quality-dependent.
rows.best practice: Inference: use Beam for designed local streaks, acknowledging that it is a different effect.

rows.key properties and values: TonemapperPreset Default/Retro.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Lighting-only; most recently parented instance wins.
rows.best practice: Inference: do not treat it like stackable, camera-local color correction.

rows.key properties and values: CurrentCamera.CFrame; FieldOfView 1–120°, default 70; CameraType; render-step scheduling.
rows.limits and mobile cost: No named universal shake amplitude/duration found here. Defaults can fight manually assigned CFrame.
rows.best practice: Inference: layer offset into camera controller, offer reduction/off, reset and unbind on cancellation.

rows.key properties and values: Engine QualityLevel 1–21; saved player setting 1–10; Automatic.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Platform-specific particle/trail/post-effect scaling. The two enums are not interchangeable.
rows.best practice: Inference: test low, high and automatic on actual devices; essential information survives each.

rows.key properties and values: PNG with alpha suits particles; general texture upload allowance up to 4096×4096; streaming varies detail.
rows.limits and mobile cost: Current texture page has conflicting UV 1024 wording; particle effective 4K not established.
rows.best practice: Inference: record source dimensions and tested runtime quality separately; reuse asset IDs.

rows.feature: Unsupported native controls in inspected API
rows.key properties and values: No dedicated chromatic-aberration, radial-blur, refraction/distortion post effect; no ParticleEmitter depth-fade or per-cell duration property found.
rows.limits and mobile cost: This is an inspected-public-API finding, not proof that every approximation is impossible.
rows.best practice: Inference: use authored overlays, separate stages, mesh silhouettes or approved existing assets; never relabel Gaussian blur as radial blur.

outputs.title: Effect card template

fields.instruction: What is it? What does it do? How large or consequential is its actual impact? Name the gameplay state the player must understand.

Record separate caster, ally and enemy ratings on the project’s chosen scale. Riot documents 1–10; no universal mapping to size, value, duration or count is established. Record why this cue outranks its neighbors.
Name the event and intended feeling. Distinguish information that must be perceived from optional embellishment.
Event source, position, direction, area/hitbox, activation and expiry, targetability, cancellation and prediction/reconciliation behavior. Decorative shape cannot silently change any of these.
Caster, ally, enemy, spectator, distance, camera angle, occlusion rules and privacy of information. State which secondary layers each audience can omit.
Asset IDs and rights; flipbook grid, frame count, resolution per cell, intended rate, loop/one-shot mode, premultiplication/edge assumptions, and whether random start preserves meaning.
Identify the single dominant shape, focal point, direction, source and target. Record small-screen and grayscale checks.
Dominant palette, accent, core/edge relationship, stage backgrounds, team/rarity/status redundancy. Use project measurements; no universal ratios established.

List primary, secondary and tertiary layers with each layer’s communication purpose, emitter/beam/trail/part/light type, orientation, attachment, and stop condition. Remove roles duplicated without benefit.

Windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through and dissipation. Store durations in seconds or ms with their source and context; if frames, store the relevant fps/timebase. Unsupported values remain unset, not zero.
Start/end size, life curves, speed, acceleration, arcs, overlap, squash/stretch, rotation, inherited motion and world/camera alignment. State how they affect the intended feeling.

Named sound event, visual sync landmark, trigger timestamp, intended relative offset, source-supported tolerance if available, and measured latency on target device. Keep network arrival separate from asset timing.
Shake/kick/zoom/flash/blur/slow motion: scope, affected player, optionality, accessibility controls and restoration behavior. Omit if it impairs the required task.
Allowed variants, semantic invariants, aggregation/cooldown/cap policy, combo escalation rule and reset condition. No count, delay or step size is a universal default.
Worst-case simultaneous events, competing critical cues, stage palette, overlap footprint and resolution when cues conflict.
Full recorded-sequence flash testing method/result; reduced motion/flash effects; colour alternatives; preserved gameplay information. No numeric pass is treated as a medical guarantee.

Target devices/graphics levels; observed frame time and frame-time spikes; transparent coverage; active/emitted particles; texture residency; lights; instancing/pool cleanup. Hardware and measurement method are required.
Describe what remains at each project quality tier. Preserve truth, timing and threat boundaries before retaining sparks, smoke, bloom or light.
Moment; symptom; evidence/capture; concrete parameter or phase change; expected result; priority; retest outcome. Change a stated cause, not merely “more polish.”
Source IDs and claim IDs; evidence level per claim; inferred values and test results; unresolved gaps; owner/version/date; pass/fail against the required checks.

intro: Start here before selecting assets or reviewing a finished effect. The card records facts, choices and evidence separately so a later designer can explain each change.

outputs.title: Review checklist
ranked_fix_order: Truth: correct actionable area and timing.
Communication: identity, consequence, magnitude and importance.
Visibility: shape, value, clutter and background compatibility.
Theme and polish after prior gates pass.

checks.step: 1 Write the communication job and viewers.
checks.pass: Identity, consequence, magnitude, audience and timing authority are explicit.
checks.if failed: Resolve missing gameplay facts before polishing.

checks.step: 2 Block in with available simple parts.
checks.pass: Primary silhouette and temporal sequence read without rich textures or glow.
checks.if failed: Swap to coarse library assets/meshes and retime the core.

checks.step: 3 Check truth first.
checks.pass: Authoritative area, contact and active interval are accurately represented in every variant.
checks.if failed: Fix semantic geometry/timing before hierarchy or theme.

checks.step: 4 Check importance and meaning.
checks.pass: Viewers identify the effect and choose the intended response relative to competing cues.
checks.if failed: Change focal region or viewer-specific priority.
checks.evidence: industry practice; test inference; ES-S02, ES-S03

checks.step: 5 Frame-step each phase.
checks.pass: No accidental pop, reversal, mismatched hit or misleading final active frame.
checks.if failed: Adjust one responsible parameter/layer, then replay at normal speed.
checks.evidence: industry practice; test inference; ES-S18, ES-S09

checks.step: 6 Inspect slow playback and timing curves.
checks.pass: Windup, punch/crescendo, follow-through and dissipation have deliberate transitions.
checks.if failed: Retune the core phase; avoid assuming slow playback itself proves good feel.
checks.evidence: industry practice; test inference; ES-S07, ES-S11

checks.step: 7 Inspect grayscale, silhouette and squint/small view.
checks.pass: Actionable geometry and primary form survive loss of hue/detail.
checks.if failed: Repair value/shape separation; keep colour semantics redundantly encoded.

checks.step: 8 Test actual phone size and graphics quality.
checks.pass: Recognition and required cues survive intended device, distance and reduced-polish conditions.
checks.if failed: Use a simpler variant and repeat performance/accessibility review.

checks.step: 9 Test bright, dark and busy stages.
checks.pass: No permitted background or camera angle erases the primary message.
checks.if failed: Adjust stage support or contrast treatment.

checks.step: 10 Test the crowded scene.
checks.pass: Targets, path, pickups and essential UI remain understandable during credible overlaps.
checks.if failed: Trim irrelevant audiences, ornamental layers, residue or simultaneous onsets.

checks.step: 11 Test with sound on and off.
checks.pass: Picture communicates its required meaning alone; audiovisual peak does not contradict contact.
checks.if failed: Separate visual/readability failure from sound-sync failure.

checks.step: 12 Review comfort and safety jointly with other effects.
checks.pass: Required accessibility checks and reduced-effect settings pass; camera control remains usable.
checks.if failed: Block release for unresolved safety/accessibility failures.
checks.evidence: inference; safety criteria supplied by Output 3 safety and synchrony section;

checks.step: 13 Polish theme only after communication passes.
checks.pass: Theme enhances the same meaning and does not recreate clutter or ambiguity.
checks.if failed: Revert polish that regresses earlier checks.

checks.step: 14 Record a reproducible comparison.
checks.pass: Before/after share gameplay seed, camera and competing effects, with precise measurements.
checks.if failed: Capture comparable evidence and state uncertainty.

checks.step: 15 A warning is readable without flipbook motion/post effects
checks.pass: Critical area, timing and identity still communicated in fallback
checks.if failed: Correct the specified failure and rerun the affected scene and device cases.

checks.step: 16 The sheet does not skip its meaningful onset
checks.pass: First meaningful/contact frame aligns with timeline, including empty cells and random-start policy
checks.if failed: Correct the specified failure and rerun the affected scene and device cases.

checks.step: 17 Every cosmetic layer has a role
checks.pass: Removing a layer has a named perceptual cost; no redundant duplicate smoke/glow
checks.if failed: Correct the specified failure and rerun the affected scene and device cases.
checks.evidence: inference informed by industry practice; RB38

checks.step: 18 Performance survives concurrency and sustained play
checks.pass: Project-agreed frame/memory envelope met on baseline device through 10–15-minute active test
checks.if failed: Correct the specified failure and rerun the affected scene and device cases.

checks.step: 19 The effect ends and can be interrupted
checks.pass: No frozen particles, old trails, lights, highlights, callbacks or camera offsets survive cleanup
checks.if failed: Correct the specified failure and rerun the affected scene and device cases.

checks.step: 20 Composite flash and reduced motion review
checks.pass: Machine safety preflight passes the selected standard/version and tested footage; critical state remains readable with optional shake, blur and flash reduced.
checks.if failed: Redesign failure before participant exposure; settings and warnings alone do not fix hazardous output.
checks.evidence: industry practice and test inference; SA01, SA02, SA03, SA04

intro: Block in the primary shapes and timing before polishing. The requested four-part repair order separates communication/importance from visibility for review convenience; it is not presented as Riot’s verbatim list. Safety and performance are release gates throughout.

profiles.application: Avoid max-tier reward spectacle on every click; test repetition and motivation instead of assuming escalation helps.

profiles.profile: Structural change is the primary event; sell mass with large pieces, cause-following secondary breaks and material response.

profiles.main risk: Dust and overlapping debris can hide traversal; preserve escape routes and surviving targets.

profiles.priorities: Truthful telegraph, trackable projectile, contact result, owner/team distinction.

profiles.profile: The current lethal hazard and safe route have priority over spectacle.
profiles.priorities: Truthful hazard boundary/state, directional threat, structural change and navigation.

profiles.evidence level: inference: proposed project profile, not validated genre-wide numeric defaults

outputs.title: Glossary

terms.definition: The information and decisions the effect must support, including identity, action and consequence.
The silhouette and arrangement of masses that make an effect recognizable.
The light-to-dark structure, independent of hue.
Hue, saturation and their relationships within the effect and scene.
How visual change is distributed through the effect’s life and aligned to events.
Arrangement and hierarchy that directs attention within an effect and across the scene.
The preparatory phase before the main action; often anticipation.
Preparation that makes the following action expected and legible.
The concentrated high-intensity accent of the action or contact.
A build in intensity toward a peak; it need not appear in every effect.
Motion that continues after the principal action as energy transfers and resolves.
The designed ending in which the effect disperses or loses prominence.
Acceleration and deceleration that make timing nonuniform.
Changing proportion to communicate deformation, motion or force while preserving intended volume impression.
A curved motion path used to organize gesture or flow.
Related components move or settle at different times rather than as one rigid unit.
The recognizable outer shape, assessable without texture detail.
The dominant directional gesture of an effect or movement.
The dominant mass or gesture carrying the effect’s essential meaning.
A supporting component that strengthens the primary action without displacing it.
Fine supporting ornament; usually a candidate for reduction before primary information.
Fragmenting a solid shape or texture into irregular pieces.
Progressive removal of a shape, often through a mask, rather than uniform transparency.
A spatially varying disappearance driven by a pattern or threshold.
A post effect that spreads bright areas into surrounding pixels; it is not geometry or a damage boundary.
An appearance of self-illumination; in Roblox light emission alone does not mean light cast onto the scene.
Combining light contributions by addition, tending to brighten overlapping regions.
Combining foreground and background using transparency; ordering and overlap matter.
A sequence of images stored in a sheet or atlas and played as animation.
An image atlas containing individual frames or sprites.
An animation intended to play through once per event.
Animation that repeats; its end-to-start transition needs design.
A new drawing or pose on each frame of the stated base timebase.
A drawing or pose held for two frames of the stated base timebase; not inherently 2 fps.
Changing the number of held base frames between image updates.
A brief graphic accent at impact, which may change silhouette, colour or contrast.
A brief pause or hold associated with contact; clarify whether simulation, animation or only presentation stops.
A held image or pose; it may be cinematic rather than a gameplay-wide pause.
A directional camera displacement or rotation linked to an event.
Time-varying camera or screen movement used to reinforce an event.
In Eiserloh’s camera model, a state variable accumulated by events and decayed over time to drive shake nonlinearly.
A cue announcing an action or hazard before activation.
The gameplay geometry used to determine contact or damage; its visual indicator must represent it truthfully.
How strongly an item attracts attention relative to its context.
Impaired identification of a target because nearby visual elements interfere, especially in peripheral vision.
Visual competition that makes relevant information harder to locate or identify.
Repeated shading of overlapping pixels; broad transparent layers can make cost high.
Level of detail; a project’s method for reducing presentation cost while preserving essential information.
Avoiding rendering or updating content that is not needed under defined visibility or relevance conditions.
Reusing instances rather than repeatedly creating and destroying them; requires reliable reset and cleanup.
A flat element oriented toward the camera or another defined direction.
Information that helps communicate distance, layering or spatial relationships.
A Roblox local reference frame used to place or connect components.
A Roblox connection rendered between attachments, useful for continuous paths and arcs.
A Roblox strip generated from attachment movement over time.
A ParticleEmitter rendering-depth offset; it does not move gameplay geometry.
A ParticleEmitter control affecting particle simulation speed, separate from global gameplay time.
Common shorthand for automated photosensitive-epilepsy flash/pattern analysis; tool, version and recorded sequence must be specified.
Combining and adapting existing parts into a new effect rather than authoring every component from scratch.
Testing the main shapes, motion and timing before texture/detail polish.
Capacity to process screen pixels; a few large sprites can cost more than many tiny ones.
Compositing that preserves occluding color according to opacity.
A lower-resolution texture representation used at smaller projected sizes or under resource constraints.
Roblox flipbook mode that fits a complete cell sequence across the particle lifetime.
A drawing held for two frames of a stated presentation frame rate; not a universal update frequency.

intro: Definitions use established field terms. Cadence requires an explicit base frame rate; a frame count alone is not a duration. Engine property names remain distinct from perceptual quantities.

outputs.title: Gaps

gaps.what remains unknown: No validated light/heavy/reward phase-duration table transfers across genres, cameras and input cadences.
gaps.how to test: Compare timing variants while holding asset art and sound fixed. Measure contact identification, response performance, perceived weight, preference and fatigue. Store display fps, capture fps, game timebase and actual ms.

gaps.what remains unknown: Riot’s importance scale does not publish a universal mapping to size, luminance, duration or layer count.
gaps.how to test: Establish ranked simultaneous-cue tasks; vary one prominence channel at a time; test whether participants identify the most consequential event correctly.

gaps.what remains unknown: Named examples and models are not safe default amplitudes, frequencies or durations for Roblox.
gaps.how to test: Test device/camera-specific variants with optional controls; measure aim/navigation errors, comfort and hit identification alongside perceived impact. Keep gameplay freeze distinct from animation-only hold.

gaps.what remains unknown: A legal or technical threshold is not an artistic target or guarantee of medical safety.
gaps.how to test: Analyze full-screen recordings of overlapping effects at worst viewing conditions; record test method/version and results. Test reduced-flash variants and seek specialist review when risk remains.

gaps.what remains unknown: No universal maximum count or screen percentage establishes readability across effects.
gaps.how to test: Stress the intended busiest scene; vary transparent footprint, overlap and importance distribution; measure target identification, hazard avoidance and frame-time percentiles.

gaps.what remains unknown: No device-independent particle, light, layer, texture-residency or frame-time budget is established.
gaps.how to test: Profile representative low-end devices and actual graphics settings. Capture worst overlaps and long sessions; derive project budgets from measured bottlenecks.

gaps.what remains unknown: The cited juice studies are not direct validation for simulator monetization loops or a common-to-legendary reveal ladder.
gaps.how to test: Compare clear restrained feedback with alternatives using comprehension, enjoyment and repeated-session measures. Do not infer player welfare or long-term retention from a short experiment.

gaps.what remains unknown: No validated variant count, randomization range, cooldown, combo step size or reset duration transfers universally.
gaps.how to test: Use repeated exposure with semantic invariants held fixed. Track recognition, fatigue, perceived consistency and task interference; test aggregation and attenuation as separate interventions.

gaps.what remains unknown: Psychophysical detection windows are task- and stimulus-dependent, not a plug-in latency budget.
gaps.how to test: Measure actual display/audio onset together on target devices; assess detection and impact under realistic input/network timing. Compare offsets without altering sound identity or visual intensity.

gaps.what remains unknown: Simple emotion labels for circles, triangles or hues are not universal causal laws.
gaps.how to test: Test the project vocabulary with unfamiliar players and accessibility modes; distinguish learned convention from direct recognition and cultural association.

gaps.what remains unknown: Upload size does not guarantee runtime resident size or effective visible resolution for every asset path.
gaps.how to test: Inspect actual particle appearance and available memory measurements on target devices; compare cell sizes and projected size, including compression, edges and mip behavior.

gaps.what remains unknown: Film on-twos/on-sixes practice does not establish a Roblox implementation or gameplay benefit.
gaps.how to test: Compare duplicated atlas frames, external sequence control and smooth playback for the same asset; measure tracking and silhouette readability. Preserve authoritative gameplay timing.

gaps.what remains unknown: Some requested candidate titles lack publicly read, maker-attributed breakdowns. Abstracts, portfolios and fan footage cannot substitute for detailed production evidence.
gaps.how to test: Prioritize direct creator interviews/talk recordings for anime, Roblox exemplars and underrepresented juicy games. Add only claims actually documented in accessible material.

gaps.what remains unknown: Available short-term or correlational results cannot establish thousands-of-plays comfort, accessibility, retention or spending effects.
gaps.how to test: Run longitudinal, consented tests with stable gameplay and participant-controlled effects; predefine outcomes and report attrition rather than selecting favorable metrics.

gaps.what remains unknown: Laboratory attention and crowding findings do not directly prescribe a game’s luminance or saturation ratios.
gaps.how to test: Use realistic scenes with competing tasks, alternative palettes and multiple camera distances; measure detection and false positives, then document the project-specific range.
